packing: Each embedding is a unit-norm float32 vector of dim values. For every vector the scale is max(abs(v)) / 127; q = round(v / scale) as int8 in [-127, 127]. The q of all vectors are concatenated in order, row-major, and base64 encoded. Decode vector i as v[j] = scale[i] * int8(q[i * dim + j]), j from 0 to dim - 1. Cosine similarity is the dot product after re-normalising the decoded vector.

passages.head: Purpose
passages.text: Knowledge recombination research measures novelty from patent classification codes and reads that classification as a dated record of what was invented. It is not one. It is a codified organisational memory, maintained for retrieval and revised after the outcomes it is used to explain. This paper asks what such a record does to the measurements taken from it.

passages.head: Design/methodology/approach
passages.text: The association between recombinant novelty and patent grant is estimated on 833,267 US applications under dated states of their own classification record, at publication and as it stands today. Documents, outcome and construction rule are held fixed, so only the state of the record varies. Seven kill tests were preregistered and frozen, each with a smallest effect of interest and a mechanical decision rule.

passages.head: Findings
passages.text: The association is +3.53pp read from today’s record and -.60pp read from the record as published. Of the +4.27pp contrast between the two conventional measures, the vintage contributes +3.90pp and the counting rule +.37pp. Outcome-blind revision would move the association only +.34pp. The decisive test failed: post-decision information is related to the decision, but within the preregistered equivalence region, and 52.1% of granted records’ change is written at the grant itself.

passages.head: Originality
passages.text: One record, two of its own dates, the same applications, with the explanation exposed to preregistered tests that are reported when they fail.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: On 833,267 US patent applications, the association between recombinant novelty and grant is +3.53pp when novelty is counted from the classification record as it stands today, and -.60pp when the same count is taken from the record the office printed at their publication. Read one way, novel recombination is associated with a higher chance of grant; read the other, with a lower one. Figure 1 sets out the design.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: Research on knowledge recombination reads patent classification codes as proxies for the components an invention joins (Fleming, 2001), dates them to the invention and counts as new any combination of codes absent from a reference set of earlier documents (Arts and Veugelers, 2015; Strumsky and Lobo, 2015; Verhoeven et al., 2016; Ju et al., 2024). The inference needs the record to hold still. It does not, and where this literature addresses revision it treats the current codes as authoritative (Arts and Veugelers, 2015; Verhoeven et al., 2016). The Cooperative Patent Classification, like the US Patent Classification it replaced (Lafond and Kim, 2019), is maintained for present retrieval: symbols are created, merged and retired, classified documents are moved to the revised scheme, and a granted application is classified again at its own decision. Figure 2 tracks the consequence: on 656,961 granted applications with a grant-time record, mean new code pairs run 2.85 at publication, 12.28 at grant and 20.95 today. The same risk arises wherever a codified memory maintained for retrieval, a record for the present (Bowker, 2005), is read as a dated history; this paper tests it on one such memory.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: The design reads one maintained record at more than one of its own dates, as real-time analysis reads revised economic data by vintage (Croushore, 2011), holding the documents, the outcome and the construction rule fixed and varying only the vintage. On the same 833,267 first filings, the two conventional measures differ in vintage and in the kinds of code they count and stand +4.27pp apart; a Shapley decomposition of that contrast (Figure 3) gives the vintage +3.90 and the counting rule +.37, the second not distinguishable from zero (p .0801).

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: Because the explanation under test was the authors’ own, seven kill tests, a reproduction gate and the decomposition were preregistered and frozen before estimation, each with its sample, model and smallest effect of interest, together with the rule that reads them; applied mechanically, that rule returned partial support. Nothing below is identified causally, and neither state of the record is treated as correct.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: Two results carry the surviving claim. The vintage difference is not what outcome-blind maintenance would produce: permuting the grant within cells of cohort, field and the publication-time state of the record moves the gap by +.34pp, and the observed movement exceeds that benchmark by +3.79pp (p .0001). And among 611,888 granted applications, carrying a symbol introduced after the five-year citation window closed rises by +1.55pp per standard deviation of forward citations, which accrued before the symbol existed.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: The decisive test failed. Using the validity date every symbol carries, it asked whether classification information that provably postdates a decision is related to that decision. It is, at +.40pp on a base of 13.87%, but the 90% interval lies inside the equivalence region fixed beforehand, which the frozen rule records as a kill. Reclassification after the decision does not explain the vintage difference. What the evidence supports is more ordinary: the writing of the record and the decision share a schedule, and on those 656,961 granted records 52.1% of the whole change is present at the grant itself, in a classification pass a refused application never receives. The proposition that later information carries the outcome is therefore supported in the aggregate and not for the individual record.

passages.head: Introduction
passages.text: The contribution is that design: read against an outcome-blind benchmark, it shows whether a measure taken from a codified memory is also a measure of that memory’s maintenance.

passages.head: Memory as store and as resource
passages.text: Walsh and Ungson (1991) located organisational memory, information from an organisation’s history, in individuals and beyond them, in culture, transformation procedures, structures and the workplace, and elaborated it through acquisition, retention and retrieval. On a strict storage reading, narrower than theirs, an entry changes only by addition or loss, so a record read today shows what was known at the date it describes. Quantitative work on codified artefacts can proceed on that reading even where revision is disclosed: one study in this journal treats classified patents as a record of recombination while placing patents invented before 2006 in a subclass created that year (Kim et al., 2026, p. 64).

passages.head: Memory as store and as resource
passages.text: A reconstructive reading treats a record as a resource for the present rather than a container of the past. Bowker (2005) develops this reading for the sciences, where the past is reconfigured as a tool for supporting the present. That reading does not deny retention; it denies that retention is all that happens to an entry, and it makes the date of reading part of what the entry means. No study we found applies both readings to one object; applied to a codified record an organisation keeps and revises, the two yield different, testable predictions about what a measurement taken from it represents.

passages.head: Codification decides what the memory can hold
passages.text: Cowan et al. (2000) treat the boundary between what is codified and what is not as set by incentive, not by the nature of the knowledge alone, so what reaches a record is the portion somebody had a reason to write down. Zollo and Winter (2002) place codification among the deliberate and effortful learning mechanisms and note that organisations invest in it to very different degrees. The documented record therefore holds what has been articulated and not the tacit knowledge used alongside it (Smith, 2001), and codified knowledge is only the tip of the iceberg of what is known (Nonaka, 1994). Applying a category to a case is an act of situated judgement exercised within collectively interpreted rules (Tsoukas and Vladimirou, 2001), and the categories themselves make some features of a case visible while leaving others unrepresented (Bowker and Star, 1999, p. 5; Star and Bowker, 2007), so a coded zero reflects the scheme and the writing effort as well as the case.

passages.head: Kept up to date, not kept still
passages.text: Classification systems are a clear case of codified memory that an organisation deliberately maintains. Bowker and Star (1999) describe them as infrastructure: built on an installed base, changed in modular increments, and invisible in use until they break down. This paper turns their argument about history (p. 41) into a measurement: the past can be reached only through classification systems, and the categories available now are not those available then.

passages.head: Kept up to date, not kept still
passages.text: In the setting studied here the upkeep is scheduled and contractual, and revision projects are published. The US office procures the reclassification of already-classified documents from contractors under a 10% maximum error rate, and a federal audit records four of them averaging 11.9%, 21.6%, 22.7% and 28.2% at inspection (US Department of Commerce, Office of Inspector General, 2023). Nothing in that arrangement ties the revision of one record to what happened to that record, although the areas chosen for revision may follow success (Arts and Veugelers, 2015, p. 1227). Outcome-blind maintenance is therefore the null against which outcome dependence has to be shown.

passages.head: One record, several dated states
passages.text: Maintenance is continuous while the events a record describes are not, so one document accumulates several states of its own entry. Strumsky and Lobo (2015) note that a new code in the US Patent Classification is applied retroactively: the office reviews granted patents and assigns the code to those meeting its criteria. Lafond and Kim (2019) document this in the same scheme: series reconstructed on the current scheme differ from historical data, the share of patents in a different main class now than at grant can be high for older cohorts, and reclassified patents tend to be more cited than those that were not.

passages.head: One record, several dated states
passages.text: The patent record is used here because its earlier states are published and dated rather than inferred. Figure 2 draws them on two lanes: the record of a granted application is written in instalments, at publication, again at the grant and then maintained; that of an application disposed of without a grant is written once and then maintained, and still grows. A measure can therefore inherit an outcome without any revision made in its light, if the writing and the outcome share a schedule.

passages.head: Secondary users and two cautions
passages.text: The users at issue are those who take a record assembled for administration and read it for research, without having taken part in constructing its codes; those who do take part interpret and use codes more similarly (Hall, 2006). Validity attaches to their inference, not to the indicator (Cronbach and Meehl, 1955), and validation in one context does not imply validity in another (Adcock and Collier, 2001). In psychology, decisions about how a construct is operationalised are a large and largely ignored source of researcher degrees of freedom (Flake and Fried, 2020); the state of the record a measure is read from is such a decision. Arts and Veugelers (2015, p. 1227) state the problem against their own design: classification updates create new subclasses and subclass combinations after filing, and such ex post reclassification is likely related to the success of the inventions concerned, although their checks found no evidence that it biased their estimates (p. 1240).

passages.head: Secondary users and two cautions
passages.text: Two cautions shape the design. First, neither state of the record is a gold standard: reading past documents through the categories their authors had and through categories developed since are both important (Bowker and Star, 1999, pp. 41-42), and the current state may describe the technology better. The record as published is only an earlier state of the same maintained system, and the claim tested is not that either state is correct. Second, a sign reversal is not by itself evidence of outcome dependence. Measurement error unrelated to the outcome can still reverse a trend across a binned exposure (Dosemeci et al., 1990), so an observed movement has to be compared with what outcome-blind maintenance alone would produce.

passages.head: Three propositions
passages.text: Each proposition comes with the observation that would refute it; each test was fixed before estimation.

passages.head: Three propositions
passages.text: *P1. Vintage.* With documents, outcome and construction rule fixed, a novelty measure built from the current record is more positively associated with the outcome than the same measure built from the record as published. *Refuted by* a type-matched vintage difference below 1pp.

passages.head: Three propositions
passages.text: *P2. Outcome dependence.* Revision of a record is related to what happened to that record and not merely later than it. The proposition can hold in the aggregate and fail for the individual entry, hence two refutation conditions. *Refuted in the aggregate by* a vintage difference no larger than outcome-blind revision would produce, with content, field, cohort and the publication-time record held fixed. *Refuted at the level of the record by* an association between provably post-decision classification information and the decision that falls inside a preregistered band of practical equivalence.

passages.head: Three propositions
passages.text: *P3. Reconstruction.* Part of the revision is related to what the field later made of the invention. *Refuted by* revision that postdates a closed observation window and is unrelated to the later recognition of the individual record.

passages.head: Three propositions
passages.text: The three ask progressively more of the evidence and are not equally supported. P1 is a measurement claim and needs no account of why the office writes what it writes. P2 separates a store from a record whose writing schedule is tied to the process under study. P3, the strongest, is examined in one channel only and would not license a claim that the office rewrites the history of successful cases.

passages.head: Empirical setting and record vintages
passages.text: The Cooperative Patent Classification, maintained jointly by the European Patent Office and the United States Patent and Trademark Office, is revised continuously. Two features of the setting matter more than its subject. Every symbol carries a validity date (EPO and USPTO, 2026), so the date a category came into existence is recorded rather than inferred. And the office publishes one document’s classification at more than one date, so the same applications can be observed under several dated states of one scheme.

passages.head: Empirical setting and record vintages
passages.text: The argument rests on the schedule of this maintenance, not its measured error (section 2.3): the record is written on its own schedule and read by secondary users as a record of the past.

passages.head: Empirical setting and record vintages
passages.text: In the 896,097 first filings of Figure 2, filed 2013 to 2017 and granted or terminally abandoned, the dated states arrive in a fixed order. An application is published 18 months after filing, a median of 549 days, and what the office prints then is the record as published. The first examiner action follows at a median 689 days for later-granted applications and 726 for later-abandoned ones; allowance comes at a median 983 days and the grant at 1,106, while an application not allowed reaches terminal abandonment at a median 1,185 days. A granted application’s classification is reviewed when it is passed to issue (USPTO, 2024, section 905.03(b)), which produces the grant-time record; an application that is not granted never receives that pass. Both records are maintained to the snapshot read here, early 2025, a median 3,298 days after filing for granted applications and 3,383 for abandoned ones. Figure 2 draws the two lanes on this axis; Table I states what each vintage can and cannot contain.

passages.head: Empirical setting and record vintages
passages.text: The population is 4,267,906 US applications filed between 2005 and 2018, published after filing, carrying at least one classification pair in PatentsView (USPTO, 2025) and matched to a prosecution history in the 2022 release of the Patent Examination Research Dataset (Graham et al., 2018; Miller, 2020); 1,265,191 of them had no grant at the December 2024 data cut. The primary sample is narrower, because the file holding the classification as published opens only around 2013 and each application must have been disposed of, and published before its own decision. Of 1,186,784 utility first filings carrying 2 to 25 scorable publication-time symbols of each type, 896,728 were filed 2015 to 2018, 875,870 of those had been disposed of by the cut, and 833,267 were published strictly before their own decision, so every publication-time record in the sample precedes its own outcome (Table S1 gives every step). The 2013 and 2014 cohorts are left out because their publication-time records are thin: 59.3% of 2013 filings carry fewer than two scorable inventional symbols, so keeping them would select on classification richness.

passages.head: Empirical setting and record vintages
passages.text: The outcome is the grant. It is a decision that part of the recombination literature sets out to explain (Ferguson and Carnabuci, 2017), the prosecution history dates it to the day, and it is observed for filings that failed as well as those that succeeded, which a collection of granted patents cannot offer (Carley et al., 2015; Sampat and Williams, 2019). It also falls between two of the three vintages, so before and after are timestamp comparisons rather than figures of speech.

passages.head: The measure
passages.text: The classification symbols on a document are read as proxies for the components an invention joins (Fleming, 2001) and taken in pairs (Verhoeven et al., 2016); the measure is the number of those pairs that appear on no earlier published document. Earlier is judged against a baseline of 48.5 million distinct pairs from 450 million pair instances on granted patents and pre-grant publications. Applications are compared in two bins, no new pair and five or more; other cuts enter section 7.

passages.head: What is held fixed and what is varied
passages.text: The same 833,267 applications, grant indicator, pairing rule, baseline and bins are used in section 5; only the classification version the pairs are drawn from changes. The design therefore compares two versions of one record, measuring neither against the truth; the current one is what the scheme’s maintainers intend a user to read today.

passages.head: What is held fixed and what is varied
passages.text: The two conventional measures differ in two choices at once: the type, whether to count inventional symbols only or every symbol, and the vintage, whether to read them from the current record or the record as published. Their contrast therefore mixes a property of the record with one of the counting rule. All four cells are estimated, the contrast is decomposed in both orders, and the Shapley average is reported so that no ordering is imposed (Shorrocks, 2013).

passages.head: Dating the information
passages.text: Two constructions make after the decision provable rather than asserted. An anachronistic code is a current code whose symbol’s validity date postdates the document’s own publication; among pre-grant publications filed 2013 to 2018, excluding the Y cross-reference scheme, 14.42% of current code assignments are anachronistic and 37.66% of documents carry at least one. The condition is weak, because a symbol can postdate a publication and still precede the decision.

passages.head: Dating the information
passages.text: The stronger construction, the post-horizon code, rests on a cohort horizon at 1 January of the sixth year after filing, and the dating tests use only applications disposed of strictly before it, so a post-horizon symbol, one whose validity begins between the horizon and 31 December 2024, could not have been on the record at the decision. Such a code counts as anchored to the document’s own earlier content when its main group, or a predecessor in a lineage map of 71,256 links over 17,107 symbols, is already in the publication-time record; it is a replacement where the current record has dropped a publication-time symbol in the same area, and an addition otherwise. Exposure to scheme revision, the share of publication-time symbols later deleted or whose main group later gained a symbol, is built from the publication-time record and the scheme history alone, so it ignores the document’s own later record and serves as both control and dose. Figure 4 reports the resulting test.

passages.head: Estimation
passages.text: Every estimate is a linear probability model with absorbed fixed effects (Guimarães and Portugal, 2010), by default measure by filing year by technology field, with cluster-robust standard errors on the 35 WIPO technology fields. Because the clusters are few, every deciding p-value is a two-sided restricted wild cluster bootstrap (Cameron et al., 2008) with Webb weights (Webb, 2023) and 9,999 draws, in which the cluster-masked residuals are re-projected through the fixed effects before the score is rebuilt, and intervals are obtained by inverting that test. For rare revision outcomes, the deciding p is the larger of the bootstrap p and a cluster-robust p over publication-time primary subclasses. Multiplicity is handled by Holm’s (1979) step-down procedure within two preregistered families. Nothing in the design identifies a causal effect.

passages.head: Preregistration
passages.text: Because analytic flexibility inflates false-positive rates (Simmons et al., 2011), the analysis plan was written, frozen and hashed before any test was run, on 21 September 2026; the plan and a lock file holding its SHA-256 and the hash of every script and construction output are deposited with the replication materials. The plan fixed each sample, each dependent variable, each model and control set, the direction predicted, the smallest effect size of interest (Lakens et al., 2018), and the rule mapping results onto a verdict (Table S2). For revision outcomes the smallest effect was the larger of .5pp and 10% of the outcome’s pooled mean, computed before any outcome was read; for the rarest mechanism outcomes the floor binds. A script then applied the rule mechanically; its verdict is partial support. Five deviations were needed, all computational rather than substantive and each disclosed with its measured effect; the largest moves an interval endpoint by under one ten-thousandth of a standard error, changing no printed digit.

passages.head: The same applications, read twice
passages.text: Only the date at which the classification record is read varies: the 833,267 first filings of section 3, the grant as outcome and the pairing rule of section 4.1 are held fixed. Applications carrying five or more new pairs are compared with those carrying none, in a stacked linear specification with the fixed effects and bootstrap intervals of section 4.4.

passages.head: The same applications, read twice
passages.text: Read from the record as it stands today, the grant gap is +3.53pp; read from the record the office published, it is -.60pp (Figure 3(a)). Neither level carries an interval, deliberately: the two gaps are point estimates of different quantities, what the design identifies is the distance between them, and the interval belongs to that difference.

passages.head: Vintage or the counting rule
passages.text: The two conventional measures, all-type symbols read today and inventional symbols read at publication, differ by +4.27pp [+3.33, +5.28]. A Shapley decomposition assigns +3.90pp of that contrast, 91%, to the vintage of the record and +.37pp, 9%, to the type of code counted, the second not distinguishable from zero (p .0801). Figure 3(b) reports both with their intervals; Table II gives the four cells and the components they are built from.

passages.head: Vintage or the counting rule
passages.text: Holding the code type fixed gives a second, distinct quantity. Across the two dates the vintage difference is +4.13pp [+3.39, +4.95] on all-type symbols throughout and +3.68pp [+3.06, +4.34] on inventional symbols throughout. Both clear the preregistered 2pp support threshold, Holm-adjusted p .0007 within the verdict family, and hold on the sensitivity samples (Table S3). The +4.27pp is what two existing measures differ by, decomposed; the +4.13pp is what two dates of reading differ by with the counting rule matched.

passages.head: What outcome-blind maintenance would produce
passages.text: A record that grew with no regard to outcomes would still move the association, because the later record is larger and grows unevenly across fields and cohorts. The permutation null supplies that benchmark: the grant is permuted within cells of filing year, technology field, publication-time code count and publication-time novelty bin, and both vintage differences are recomputed 9,999 times. Outcome-blind growth moves the gap by +.34pp. The observed movement exceeds that benchmark by +3.79pp, permutation p .0001, the floor of 9,999 draws and to be read as p ≤ .0001; Table II gives the inventional counterparts.

passages.head: What outcome-blind maintenance would produce
passages.text: That excess is what makes the sign reversal interpretable. It does not say why the record moved; section 6 takes that up.

passages.head: Two qualifications
passages.text: Part of what the counted measure attributes to novelty is breadth. A count of new pairs rises with the number of symbols a record carries, and the later record carries more of them (Figure 2). With novelty defined instead as the share of an application’s pairs that are new, top decile against a share of zero, the vintage difference is +1.83pp on all-type and +.72pp on inventional symbols, against +4.93pp for the counted measure taken the same way. These are raw differences of bin means without fixed effects, comparable with each other and not with the adjusted +4.13pp. Breadth therefore carries a substantial part of what the count records, and the difference between the two readings does not disappear when breadth is taken out.

passages.head: Two qualifications
passages.text: Documents also move between bins less than the published comparison implies. Of the applications the current record places in the top novelty bin, 38.5% stay there under the publication-time record of the same type and 21.9% fall to zero (Figure 3(c)); Table IV gives the full matrix for both code types, and Figure S1 the same on the wider sample. The two conventional measures give 20.5% and 34.1%, but on a different sample of 1,520,189 publications and with the code type changed as well as the date; on that sample the reversal holds within nearly every subgroup (Figure S2).

passages.head: Why the records diverge
passages.text: Table III lists the labelled tests in the order the preregistration set, with the label the frozen rule assigned, failures beside successes. Nothing here is causal: each estimate is an association between a feature of a record and an outcome recorded on it.

passages.head: What does not explain the gap
passages.text: The explanation the literature raises for citations, and the one this paper set out to test for the grant, is that symbols introduced after a decision are applied backwards to the documents that turned out well, so that a measure read today has the outcome written into it (Fleming, 2001; Arts and Veugelers, 2015). K1, given first priority in the preregistration, tests that claim at the level of the individual record: a symbol’s validity date shows that the information could not have been on the record when the decision was taken. On 821,783 applications with a publication-time main group that later received a post-horizon symbol, 821,647 of them in the regression, granted applications are more likely than others to carry such a symbol, by +.40pp on a base of 13.87%, 90% interval [+.155, +.652], and to carry one that adds a new pair, by +.66pp on a base of 9.65%, 90% interval [+.364, +.957]. Both are precisely determined and both intervals lie inside the band of practical equivalence fixed before the tests: under the frozen rule, a kill by equivalence. The associations are real, about 3% and 7% in relative terms. Figure 4(a) draws both against their bands and 4(b) their variants (Table S4); the second lies inside its band by only about eight thousandths of a point, so it is reported with its interval and not only its label.

passages.head: What does not explain the gap
passages.text: The internal split is informative even though neither part meets the support rule. The whole association sits in additions, symbols that describe something the record did not previously say, at +.46pp on a base of 2.92%, and none in replacements, the mechanical substitution of a retired symbol, at -.05pp (p .7157). What distinguishes a granted record after the decision is new description rather than housekeeping, but too little of it to carry the result of section 5.

passages.head: What does not explain the gap
passages.text: A direct counterfactual agrees. On the 896,097 first filings of Figure 2, not section 5’s sample, the grant gap is +6.16pp read from the current record and -.36pp read from the record as published. Removing every code whose symbol postdates the application’s own disposition moves the current-record gap to +5.46pp, a change of -.70pp; removing as many randomly chosen symbols that are not post-horizon moves it to +5.56pp, a change of -.60pp (Figure 4(c)). The provably post-decision layer is worth about what arbitrary removal of the same size is worth. Nor is scheme revision the carrier: section 5’s applications whose publication-time symbols no scheme event touched still show an excess of +4.11pp over the outcome-blind null, inside the +3.04pp to +5.24pp range of the exposed quintiles and above the least exposed of them. Across those quintiles the gradient runs in the predicted direction but is not monotone, Spearman +.90, and the top-minus-bottom difference of +2.20pp does not clear its threshold (p .0642), so that test is inconclusive (Figure 5(b)).

passages.head: What does not explain the gap
passages.text: A second explanation also fails. A novelty baseline built from granted patents alone, as in Arts and Veugelers (2015), omits recombination that unsuccessful publications had already disclosed, and that omission might be expected to be selective. On 3,202,512 first filings, removing from the baseline the publications that had no grant at the data cut turns fewer pairs new than removing matched random sets of applications, by -.057 per first filing (Figure S3) [-.078, -.037], p .0001, against an equivalence threshold of .052: actual removal makes new pairs for 26.7% of first filings against 55.9% under random removal. The baseline is a construction choice with measurable consequences, not a bias of known sign. The likely reason is visible in Figure 2: today a granted application’s record carries 9.45 symbols against 8.48 for a terminally abandoned one, while at publication the two are almost the same size, 4.43 against 4.40.

passages.head: What does not explain the gap
passages.text: Two of these failed the paper’s own predictions; they narrow the surviving explanation, and the difference of section 5 depends on neither. P2, that revision is related to the outcome, is supported in the aggregate, by the excess over the permutation null, and not at the level of the individual record, where the test built to decide it returned an effect inside the preregistered band.

passages.head: What does appear to matter
passages.text: What is left is more mundane than retrospective reclassification, and better documented. On 656,961 granted applications carrying a grant-time record, mean new pairs run 2.85 at publication, 12.28 at the grant and 20.95 on the current record, so 52.1% of the whole change is present at the decision itself, in a classification pass that a refused application never receives (Figure 4(d)). The record of a refused application is not frozen: written once and then maintained, it rises from 2.95 new pairs to 17.47. What differs is the second writing event, which shares its schedule with the outcome.

passages.head: What does appear to matter
passages.text: A narrower channel does look reconstructive. Among 611,888 granted applications, granted from 2015 onward, published by mid-2019 and matched to a single patent, the probability of carrying an anchored symbol introduced after the five-year forward citation window closed rises by +1.55pp per standard deviation of log forward citations, on a base of 9.06%, bootstrap p .0001, Holm-adjusted p .0007. The timing is what makes this worth reporting: the symbol did not exist while the citations were accruing, so the citations cannot be a consequence of the classification. The preregistered rule calls it supported on the estimate and the adjusted p, but its 95% interval, [+.881, +2.234], reaches into the equivalence region, whose boundary is .906. Nine variants, seven drawn and all in Table S5, move it between +1.29pp and +1.92pp. Figure 5(a) shows it beside its companion, revision after the grant on the patent’s stock-market value (Kogan et al., 2017), which returns nothing: -.08pp per standard deviation on 180,196 granted applications with a positive market-value match, well inside an equivalence threshold of 2.635 (p .5849).

passages.head: What does appear to matter
passages.text: The third is the maintenance of family records. Descendants of an earlier filing are +62.5pp more likely than first filings to record zero novelty, on 1,550,133 first filings and 428,713 descendants. Removing the descendant’s own family documents from the prior art closes .977 (Table S6, Figure S3) [.959, .992] of that gap and leaves +1.5pp, so the zero comes from the family’s earlier documents sitting in the baseline. On the smaller set of families whose root was published in 2017 or later, 67,432 units in 30,431 families, the descendant premium is +25.9pp larger read from the current record than from the record as published [+22.8, +28.4], p .0001, although that estimate does not meet its preregistered precision check. A premium is present at publication as well, 58.0% against 49.3%, so maintenance enlarges an inheritance rather than creating it.

passages.head: An exploratory measure that cannot be reclassified
passages.text: A measure taken from a document’s text cannot be revised by the office at all. Novelty counted as the content bigrams of a published abstract that appear in no abstract published before the application’s filing date, adapted from the new-bigram measure of Arts et al. (2021), is fixed at publication by construction. The estimation sample is its top and bottom quintiles, formed within filing year, among the first filings of Figure 2 carrying a scorable abstract: 358,438 applications. The most textually novel quintile is granted less often than the least, by -8.18pp raw and -4.27pp with filing year by field fixed effects, standard error .82.

passages.head: An exploratory measure that cannot be reclassified
passages.text: The code gaps this contrast is set against, +6.16pp and -.36pp, are taken over the whole sample from which those quintiles are drawn, not over the 358,438, so the two contrasts rest on different sets of documents and can be compared in sign only. In sign, the frozen measure agrees with the record as published and disagrees with the current record. It is weak convergent evidence rather than a validation, because the agreement is directional only and text novelty is close to uncorrelated with either code measure, .004 with the current count and .022 with the publication-time count. It does not make the record as published correct, and no test here could.

passages.head: Inferential consequences
passages.text: Section 5 varies only the state of the record; the converse question is how much of the answer’s movement belongs to the record rather than to ordinary modelling latitude. The same quantity was estimated under every defensible combination of six choices: the novelty measure, which pairs the baseline with the vintage of the codes; whether related filings stay in; the filing window; the novelty cut; the control set; and whether to restrict to software-exposed fields. That gives 432 specifications drawn from 4,257,607 published applications carrying a WIPO technology field, not the 833,267 first filings of section 5. The enumeration covers data construction as well as modelling (Steegen et al., 2016).

passages.head: Inferential consequences
passages.text: In Figure 6, estimates run from -6.46pp to +14.42pp with a median of -1.31pp; 190 intervals lie entirely below zero, 187 span it and 55 lie entirely above it, none of those 55 reading novelty from the record as published. The specification closest to published practice, current codes against a granted-patent baseline with every filing retained, returns +.31pp [-2.15, +2.77] and cannot reject zero; publication-time codes with breadth controlled return -4.09pp [-5.08, -3.10]. Figure 6 marks both and presents neither as correct.

passages.head: Inferential consequences
passages.text: Many answers are available, which is by now familiar (Leamer, 1983); what matters, as in a specification curve (Simonsohn et al., 2020), is which choice carries the movement. Leverage, the largest median absolute change from swapping two levels of one choice with all else fixed, is 3.2 points for the novelty measure, 3.1 for whether related filings stay in, 3.1 for the control set, 1.9 for the novelty cut, 1.5 for the field restriction and 1.2 for the filing window (Figure 6(b)). The enumeration cannot separate the record’s vintage from the baseline or the symbol type, all three sitting crossed inside one choice. It locates the problem, and the decomposition of section 5 measures it.

passages.head: A record written in instalments
passages.text: Neither reading of organisational memory in section 2.1 fits a maintained classification. The strict storage reading is refused by the sign reversal of section 5 and by its excess over the outcome-blind null. Reconstruction (Bowker, 2005) is licensed in one channel only, the citation gradient on symbols that postdate the closed window, and it does not extend to market value.

passages.head: A record written in instalments
passages.text: What sits between them is more mundane: the record of a granted application is written again at the decision and that of a refused one is not, so a measure can inherit the outcome without anything being rewritten in hindsight. Where documentation is completed on the outcome’s schedule, as an incident report may be on escalation, a customer record when a deal closes or a case file on decision, the density of the record can track the outcome; this paper shows it for one classification only. Zollo and Winter (2002) expect codification effort to vary with the task; in this record the variation follows the outcome’s schedule and can be dated. For knowledge management the point is a dating rule rather than a new construct: a codified memory is dated by the schedule on which it was written, not by the events its entries describe, and a secondary user who reads it as a history has to recover that schedule first.

passages.head: What this asks of researchers
passages.text: The implication is not that classification is bad but that it has a maintenance history, which a secondary user making a historical claim must reconstruct. Three asks follow, in ascending cost: ask when the measure was written, not only what it says, meaning whether the categories and assignments existed at the event they are dated to; if the artefact is versioned, read two versions and state which one an estimate comes from, since a second version is a join, not a new data collection; and if it is not, ask whether the writing is coupled to the outcome, because here coupling, not revision, does the damage.

passages.head: What this asks of researchers
passages.text: Two consequences are specific to recombination measures. A count of first-time pairs also counts how broadly a document has been classified, itself a product of maintenance, so breadth belongs in the reported model. And a level read from the current record moves by more than its own size across defensible states of the record, whereas a difference can remove a component common to both its sides, a protection argued here, not demonstrated.

passages.head: What this asks of taxonomy keepers
passages.text: The keeper of this scheme already publishes most of what a historical user needs, except a date on each assignment, whose absence is why the tests here had to prove timing from the symbol’s validity date. To serve historical work, the keeper should date assignments and keep superseded states as first-class objects rather than by-products of a snapshot. Accuracy is a separate question from vintage, and not a reassuring one: the federal audit reports initial contractor classifications averaging above the contractual error maximum and accepted regardless (US Department of Commerce, Office of Inspector General, 2023). The two defects need different remedies; only the undated one is this paper’s subject.

passages.head: Objections and scope
passages.text: The first objection is that the current codes are simply better, embodying what has been learned since publication. They may well be, and a classification is in either case a negotiated and maintained artefact rather than a neutral record of what it classifies (Bowker and Star, 1999). The claim is only that the estimate moves with the state of the record, by more than outcome-blind maintenance produces.

passages.head: Objections and scope
passages.text: The second is that a sign reversal is what non-differential measurement error does to a binned exposure. Hence the reversal is not offered alone: the design adds an outcome-blind null, a grant-time record that refused applications never receive, and a text measure that cannot be reclassified and agrees in sign with the earlier state.

passages.head: Objections and scope
passages.text: The third, a genuine competitor that is not ruled out, is that the pre-examination classification is itself endogenous, since it shapes the search that decides the application. The current scheme does not show the past as contemporaries classified it (Lafond and Kim, 2019), but the converse does not make the earlier state clean, so the paper compares two imperfect states. Pre-examination classification does not account for the post-window citation gradient, measured on symbols that did not exist at the decision.

passages.head: Objections and scope
passages.text: The fourth is that the clustering is thin. Technology fields are few, hence the bootstrap of section 4.4; whether to cluster is a question about the sampling and assignment processes, not a convention (Abadie et al., 2023). Software-exposed specifications, on three field clusters, decide nothing. The scope is one office, one scheme, one outcome and one family of count-based measures, on applications published from 2013.

passages.head: Conclusion and limitations
passages.text: The scheme studied here is maintained so that the next search succeeds, and its maintenance is scheduled, documented and dated. Read as a dated history, it returns an association between recombinant novelty and grant whose sign depends on which of its own dates it is read from.

passages.head: Conclusion and limitations
passages.text: Five things cannot be claimed. Nothing here is causal: every estimate is an association, and the timing arguments establish only that information cannot have been written before an event. Reclassification after the decision does not explain the difference: the provably post-decision layer is worth about as much as an equal number of arbitrary codes. No new construct is offered: anachronism, look-ahead bias, outcome-dependent measurement error and maintenance already have names, and organisational memory theory is used, not extended. Nothing is claimed for applications published before 2013, where the record as published cannot be reconstructed from the available files. And neither state of the record is a truth against which the other can be scored.

passages.head: Conclusion and limitations
passages.text: What is left is a distinction any secondary user of a maintained artefact can act on. A record optimised for present retrieval is judged by whether the next search succeeds, and it earns its revisions. A record optimised for historical inference is judged by whether it can be read back to a date. The scheme studied here is the first kind, used as though it were the second, and the gap between the two is wider than the effect most studies of recombinant novelty set out to estimate.
